title: Rabbi Yosi bar Asyan (or Yasinia)

paragraphs: Rabbi Yose bar Asyan, or Yasinia.

In [Eruvin 53b](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.53b.11-12) they say: when Rabbi Yose bar Asyan spoke cryptically, he said, “Make me an ox in judgment on a poor mountain.” When asking about lodging, he said, “Man, mouth, this, living—what good is there?” In [Beitzah 8b](https://www.sefaria.org/Beitzah.8b.18): “Rabbi Yose bar Yasinia (in Dikdukei Soferim: Yasyan) said: this applies only where he cannot cover it,” etc. (This refers to Rabbi Zeira’s statement.) Possibly he is Yose bar Ashyan, mentioned in [Jerusalem Talmud Sukkah 4:6](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Sukkah.4.6.4) as speaking in the name of Resh Lakish. In Ha-Asif 5648, p. 189, the author proposes that this Rabbi Yose ben Asyan is the Rabbi Yose mentioned in [Jerusalem Talmud Sanhedrin 3:5](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Sanhedrin.3.5.10): “Rabbi Yonah and Rabbi Yose permitted baking for Ursicinus on Shabbat.” Hyman rejects this as an error: as is known, Rabbi Yonah’s colleague was Rabbi Yose bar Zevida, who was indeed among the leading halakhic authorities, whereas Rabbi Yose bar Asyan is not found issuing halakhic rulings. “This is clear,” he concludes.[^1][^2]

notes.text: [Rashi](https://www.sefaria.org/Rashi_on_Eruvin.53b.11.2-3) reads tor plus din as teradin (beets) and har plus dal as hardal (mustard). [Rashi’s explanation of the lodging question](https://www.sefaria.org/Rashi_on_Eruvin.53b.12.2) and [Tosafot’s quotation of Rabbenu Chananel](https://www.sefaria.org/Tosafot_on_Eruvin.53b.12.1) divide the words differently.

The Yerushalmi in Sukkah names Yose bar Ashyan speaking in the name of Resh Lakish. The baking episode names Rabbi Yonah and Rabbi Yose without a patronymic. Ha-Asif’s identification and Hyman’s rejection of it are competing readings of the evidence.
